author: Mark Atwood
text:
Sibling workspace-coordination case to JMAP-ops7.24 (metadata-server) and JMAP-ic0j.26 (calendars-server, parent workspace bead, OPEN). All three are instances of the same "spec-mandated method has permissive default impl that silently violates spec in production" anti-pattern.

**Recommendation echo: option (a) — drop the default impl.** Same rationale as JMAP-ops7.24:
1. Workspace AGENTS.md "Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED" §1 (silent-drop = server-side query-correctness bug) names the policy.
2. Canonical jmap-mail-server has no default for spec-mandated mutations (blob_exists doc-comment at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:194-198 is the workspace policy statement).
3. The bead body itself recommends this: "drop the default; require backends to provide an impl, exactly like mail-server pattern for import_email / parse_email / etc."

**Why not autonomously implement:** Public-API-breaking trait change in 3 sibling crates (per AGENTS.md "When NOT to file human" rule 3 qualifier). Workspace coordination via a single epic is the right vehicle.

**Recommended workspace shape:** File a new workspace epic that owns:
- crate-jmap-tasks-server: drop update_task_per_user default (this bead)
- crate-jmap-metadata-server: drop get_metadata_changes default (JMAP-ops7.24)
- crate-jmap-calendars-server: drop the relevant defaults (JMAP-ic0j.26)
- Update all reference MemoryBackend impls to honor the now-required methods (most already do)
- Update cookie-cutter rustdoc / sibling AGENTS.md banners

This bead and JMAP-ops7.24 close as superseded by that epic; JMAP-ic0j.26 either closes as superseded too or becomes the epic itself.
